S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report each thermal incident involving fire, smoke, or hazardous overheating to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify affected customers within 48 hours when the incident presents a credible safety risk, and promptly provide any material safety instructions.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A 5% failure rate is the per-model safety benchmark. Test results, including sample size and failure rate, must be submitted confidentially to regulators and provided to customers who own that model; individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published publicly. Regulators shall determine proportionate enforcement based on the results, corrective actions, and risk; exceeding the benchmark alone does not automatically require a sales suspension or recall.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all installed units. Manufacturers must enable the capability on units that already support it and provide a safe retrofit or equivalent compliant solution for other units within 6 years of adoption. Manufacturers must document completion and report any units that cannot be brought into compliance, with the reason and interim risk controls, to the regulator and affected customers.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units placed on the market must include built-in fire suppression meeting applicable regulator-approved performance and safety requirements, beginning 36 months after adoption.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A recall is mandatory when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers must notify regulators and affected customers without delay and provide a safe remedy.

document.section_notes: The final text keeps the 55 °C test, the 5% per-model benchmark, confidential numeric results to owners and regulators, and no public per-model publication, but removes any automatic sales stop, so a model above 5% (such as the Hearth 10 at 6.2%) is handled through regulator-determined enforcement. Remote shut-off retrofit is extended to 6 years and suppression to 36 months, both favouring the companies with lower coverage or higher suppression costs. The 8-per-100,000 mandatory recall trigger is kept with no transition, which directly reaches the Ember 8 at 9.9. The S1 text says the 10-business-day complete report is separate from the 24-hour notice; I recorded only the 24-hour deadline as the reporting parameter, and no minor-incident exclusion appears.
